articles.title: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa: Where does Old Trafford thriller rank among Premier League's greatest games?
articles.summary: Where does Manchester United 4-4 Aston Villa rank among the Premier League's greatest games?
articles.body:
When Manchester United and Aston Villa served up an eight-goal thriller at Old Trafford on Sunday afternoon, it was an instant Premier League classic.

While the match will not define either side's season, it will be remembered for years to come.

In fact, it was only the 29th time in Premier League history both teams had scored four goals each in the same match.

It was not the first time United have been involved in a high-scoring Premier League encounter, either.

Last December, the Red Devils had to settle for a share of the points against Bournemouth after another game where eight goals were shared.

And in Sir Alex Ferguson's final match in charge of United in May 2013, they drew 5-5 with West Brom at The Hawthorns.

But where does Sunday's match rank among the other remarkable matches we have witnessed down the years?

Having blown a 10-point lead at the top of the table, Newcastle 's title hopes suffered a major blow as they lost a classic in stoppage time at Anfield despite having led twice.

In an extraordinary conclusion to the 2011-12 campaign, Manchester City scored twice in stoppage time to beat Queens Park Rangers on the final day and win their first title in 44 years.

Sergio Aguero's famous late winner ensured City pipped rivals Manchester United , who had already won that day, to the trophy on goal difference.

On another remarkable evening at Anfield, Arsenal 's Andrey Arshavin produced a stunning individual display - netting all four goals for the Gunners to deliver a serious blow to Liverpool 's title ambitions.

Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa (8 November 2026)

United seemed dead and buried, not once but twice, as they trailed Europa League winners Aston Villa 2-0 and then 4-2 at Old Trafford.

But late strikes from substitutes Joshua Zirkzee and then Patrick Dorgu, deep into stoppage time, may have rescued not only a point, but Michael Carrick's job as United manager.

Arsenal were 4-0 up at and cruising at half-time as they looked to chase down league leaders Manchester United .

However, Abou Diaby was then sent off for the Gunners as Newcastle produced a stunning comeback to earn an improbable draw - with Cheick Tiote's thumping 87th-minute strike clinching the point.

With Manchester United having beaten Newcastle to the title the previous season, this felt like payback for Kevin Keegan and his players, who had also suffered a 4-0 reverse to Sir Alex Ferguson's side at Wembley in the Charity Shield just weeks earlier.

Tottenham 3-5 Man Utd (29 September 2001)

Manchester United staged a magnificent comeback from 3-0 down at the break to overwhelm Tottenham at White Hart Lane.

Dean Richards, Les Ferdinand and Christian Ziege all scored for the hosts but a transformed United hit back through Andy Cole, Laurent Blanc, Ruud van Nistelrooy, Juan Sebastian Veron and David Beckham.

Man Utd 4-3 Man City (21 September 2009)

Michael Owen's winner deep into stoppage time gave Manchester United a dramatic victory in a classic derby at Old Trafford.

The moment prompted Ferguson to set off on an impromptu wild dance along the touchline, while City boss Mark Hughes - whose side had come from behind three times - questioned why the game had gone on for six added minutes rather than the four allocated.

Liverpool had gone 2-0 up early on with goals from Sami Hyypia and Christian Ziege, but Mark Viduka scored either side of half-time to drag Leeds level.

Vladimir Smicer restored Liverpool 's advantage, before two goals in three minutes from former Celtic forward Viduka secured an incredible win for the hosts.

Crystal Palace 3-3 Liverpool (5 May 2014)

Title-chasing Liverpool had just lost to Chelsea at Anfield, but looked set to power themselves back into the race when they took a commanding 3-0 lead at Selhurst Park.

But they squandered that advantage in a chaotic final 11 minutes, leaving Luis Suarez in tears at the final whistle. Man City went on to win the league by two points.

A tight pitch, a packed Highbury and another compelling contest between two of English football's heavyweights.

The Gunners went two goals up courtesy of Nicolas Anelka and Patrick Vieira only for the champions to draw level thanks to two Teddy Sheringham efforts.

But in a season when Arsene Wenger's side were to wrestle the title away from Manchester, David Platt scored the winner.

Most people will remember this game because of the fiery exchange between captains Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane in the tunnel before the game, but the 90 minutes itself were just as thrilling.

Vieira opened the scoring for Arsenal before they were pegged back by an Ashley Cole own goal.

Another Gunners legend, Dennis Bergkamp, helped the hosts retake the lead before two goals from a young Cristiano Ronaldo and a delightful John O'Shea chip stunned Arsene Wenger's side.

A match that meant most for a side that wasn't involved - the day that Leicester City were crowned champions will go down in footballing history.

Two first-half goals from Harry Kane and Heung-min Son gave Tottenham hope of chasing the Foxes down at the business end of the season.

But Gary Cahill and Eden Hazard scored to get Jamie Vardy and his Leicester team-mates' party started as tempers flared in the second half of a match dubbed the 'Battle of the Bridge'.

Man Utd v Bournemouth (15 December 2025)

Manchester United and Bournemouth played out at a Premier League classic at Old Trafford last season.

The hosts led three times and thought they had won the game when they scored twice in 129 seconds to turn a 3-2 deficit into a 4-3 advantage.

But Eli Junior Kroupi's strike in the 84th minute pegged Ruben Amorim's side back once again as both sides had to settle for a share of the spoils.

A version of this article was first published in December 2025.

articles.title: Deion Sanders Drops Honest Quote on Colorado's 3-6 Season, Talks Hot Seat After Loss to ASU
articles.summary: Colorado head coach Deion Sanders reflected on the team's disappointing 2026 season following a 20-10 loss to Arizona State on Saturday.
articles.body:
Colorado head coach Deion Sanders reflected on the team's disappointing 2026 season following a 20-10 loss to Arizona State on Saturday.

"The season don't look good," Sanders told reporters after the game. "It don't look good. I'm not crazy. I can see clearly. You think I'm happy? I'm not happy with the outcomes. I'm not a loser by any means, and I hate the fact that we're coming up on the short end of these games."

Sanders was also asked about his job status, but he seemed unconcerned.

"Man, I don't think about that, man," the coach told reporters . "I'm not here for my job, I'm here for these young men. I'm not built like that. I'm really not. I'm really, really, really not. I want these kids to graduate, to provoke change in their communities (and) in their lives and their families. I ain't worried about me. I'm good, brother. I'm not worried about me. I worry about others. That's who I'm called to be."

The Buffaloes fell to 3-6 with Saturday's defeat, as they've lost six of their past seven games since starting the season at 2-0.

Colorado recorded just 10 points against Arizona State after entering the matchup with the worst scoring offense in the Big 12, averaging a mere 21.0 points per game through eight contests.

The Buffaloes were also held scoreless in the first half on Saturday, as they weren't able to find the end zone until they trailed 20-3 with just over eight minutes remaining in the fourth quarter.

Colorado posted a 9-4 record during Sanders' second season with the school in 2024, but the Buffaloes have gone just 6-15 in two years since.

articles.title: Pellegrini: "Este era un partido para equipo grande"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Betis, satisfecho tras la victoria de su equipo en el Martínez Valero
articles.summary: El técnico del Betis, satisfecho tras la victoria de su equipo en el Martínez Valero
articles.body: Manuel Pellegrini analizaba la victoria de su equipo frente al Elche en declaraciones a DAZN LaLiga. "Muy contento porque son tres puntos muy importantes para seguir en la parte de arriba de la tabla. Sabíamos que era un equipo contra el que era muy difícil jugar. Tuvimos mucho control e intensidad para recuperar los primeros 20 minutos. Estuvimos bastante bien pero en los últimos 25 ellos tuvieron el control del partido. Ya habíamos tenido la intensidad que se requiere antes de los goles, con dos o tres ocasiones muy claras. Muy contento por el segundo tiempo y con el plantel. Están todos muy involucrados sacando partido tras partido", comentó. Mejor en la segunda parte. "En el primer tiempo perdimos la intensidad para recuperar la pelota y, cuando la teníamos, lo hacíamos sin movilidad para hacer daño en su defensa. Los últimos 25 minutos del primer tiempo no me gustaron, pero el equipo es consciente de mejorar los aspectos del primer periodo y desde el primer minuto apretamos para apretar teniendo el control del balón y buscando la portería contraria como hay que hacerlo para ser un equipo grande". Acierto en los cambios. "Ha sido algo muy hablado con el plantel. Una cosa son los once que empiezan, pero los que entran luego son igual de importantes. Están más descansados y saben qué partido se van a encontrar. Por más que algunos critiquen las rotaciones, las hago cuando veo que los futbolistas responden en los entrenamientos al nivel que uno espera y eso me deja contento. Ahora empezamos el jueves la Copa del Rey y ojalá que veamos al mismo Betis de LaLiga y la Champions". Bartra. "Muy importante el gol para Marc. Nos da personalidad y cabecea muy bien. Igual que hay críticas por los goles que hemos recibido a balón parado, también hemos hecho. Es tan importante el que sirve la pelota como el que la finaliza". ¿Candidato al título?. "Habíamos hablado que este era un partido para equipo grande que aspira a cosas importantes. Sabemos que juegan entre ellos dos que están por arriba y que si gana el Atlético quedamos a cinco puntos. No estamos pensando más allá del próximo partido y sí tener personalidad y fútbol para demostrar que podemos estar en la parte más superior de la tabla para clasificarnos para la Champions".

articles.title: Fan hospitalised after falling through stand at Norwegian football match
articles.summary: A stand in the away end of Tromso’s stadium gave way during a match against Bodo/Glimt, causing fans to fall through.
articles.body:
Several fans were injured during a football match in Norway when a panel in the stand for travelling supporters gave way.

Fans fell through the hole at Tromso’s stadium and ⁠⁠⁠⁠one was taken to hospital during their match against Bodo/Glimt on Sunday, both clubs said.

The top division game was stopped just before half-time when Bodo keeper Nikita Haikin called the referee’s attention to the incident ‌‌‌‌behind the goal, where the away fans were standing in the pouring rain.

“We have had a serious incident in the away stand in connection with the game between TIL and Bodo/Glimt. Preliminary information is that a person has fallen through the stands and is injured,” Tromso said in a statement.

“Up to five people fell through ⁠⁠⁠⁠the stands and one was sent to hospital,” ⁠⁠⁠⁠Bodo press officer Simen Pedersen told the Reuters news agency.

The statement gave no details about the injuries.

“We stood and bounced to a supporter song, then the floor gave way; ⁠ ⁠⁠ ⁠it cracked in two in the row in front of us,” Andrine Moen, a Bodo supporter who witnessed the accident, told local newspaper Verdens Gang (VG).

“There were at least two ⁠⁠⁠⁠people who fell through the floor, but ⁠⁠⁠⁠we don’t know how far they fell or how many fell in total,” she said.

Bodo fans were instructed to leave the away section, with Tromso fans asked ‌‌‌‌to make space for them in other parts of the ground, VG reported.

Following consultations between the two teams, the Norwegian Football Federation (NFF), supporters and the police, the game resumed and Bodo’s Ola Brynhildsen scored ‌‌‌‌twice ‌‌‌‌to send his side top of the Eliteserien table, ahead of Viking Stavanger on goal difference.

articles.title: Tromso v Bodo/Glimt: Fan injured after falling through hole in away stand
articles.summary: One fan is taken to hospital after a number of Bodo/Glimt supporters fall through a hole in the away stand at Tromso.
articles.body:
A fan was taken to hospital after a number of Bodo/Glimt supporters fell through a hole in the away stand at Tromso.

The Norwegian top-flight match at Romssa Arena on Sunday was paused just before half-time after Bodo keeper Nikita Haikin called for the referee's attention.

Bodo/Glimt press officer Simen Pedersen told the Reuters news agency that "up to five people fell through the stands".

"We stood and bounced to a supporter song, then the floor gave way," Bodo supporter Andrine Moen told local newspaper Verdens Gang, as reported by Reuters.

"It cracked in two in the row in front of us. There were at least two people who fell through the floor, but we don't know how far they fell or how many fell in total."

The remaining Bodo supporters were moved into other parts of the ground before the match resumed.

The match at Tromso's stadium - the northernmost venue in Norway's Eliteserien - was played in heavy rain.

The score was 0-0 at the time of the incident, but Bodo forward Ola Brynhildsen scored twice after the game resumed to give the league leaders a 2-0 win.

Bodo are locked in a title battle with Viking and the Eliteserien season is set to finish in the first week of December.

articles.title: El Barcelona vuelve a estirar el chicle
articles.standfirst: Golea al Madrid CFF en el Johan Cruyff y amplía a cuatro puntos la diferencia con el Real Madrid
articles.summary: Golea al Madrid CFF en el Johan Cruyff y amplía a cuatro puntos la diferencia con el Real Madrid
articles.body: El Barcelona se impuso (5-1) al Madrid CFF en el Johan Cruyff ante 2.572 espectadores con tantos de Brugts, Pajor, Julià, Guijarro y Pina. El equipo dirigido por Pere Romeu amplía a cuatro puntos la diferencia respecto al Real Madrid cuando el torneo doméstico llega al primer tercio consumido. Las locales saltaron al verde como un ciclón. Pina mandó el balón al travesaño en el primer minuto en una jugada previamente anulada por asistir Schertenleib desde fuera de los límites del campo; rematando al muñeco poco después tras una asistencia de Graham desde el costado diestro. La respuesta blanca fue un disparo blando de Sakina tras un mal despeje de Cata. Tras el minuto de homenaje a Jesús de Miguel, el Barcelona volvió a dar un giro de tuerca, sobre todo por una banda derecha donde Schertenleib, Rosalía y Graham estuvieron muy activas. Las visitantes, intentando mantener el orden, apostaron todo a la velocidad a la contra de Sakina y Ubamba. La lata se acabó abriendo a seis minutos para el final del primer acto en una buena jugada trenzada en la frontal y gol de Brugts, que aprovechó un inoportuno resbalón de Mónica para batir a Belén. Nadando a favor de corriente, las locales aumentaron la renta en el añadido con un nuevo gol de Pajor, que celebró su partido 100 con el Barcelona con el tanto número 82 de azulgrana. Los cambios propuestos por Sánchez Vera tras el descanso no variaron la hoja de ruta. Entre las permutas locales salió Torrejón, que celebró su partido 500 con el Barcelona dando una asistencia -cuando sólo llevaba un minuto en el campo- a Julià para el tercero de las azulgrana. Poco después, un Guijarrazo ampliaría la distancia en el marcador y Pina, que ya lleva 11 en lo que llevamos de Liga, se uniría al festín goleador. El único lunar azulgrana llegó a siete minutos para el final con el gol de Konan, que aprovechó una asistencia de Alba para revolverse en el área y superar a Cata. La última del partido fue para Torrejón, en el añadido, rematando un córner a las manos de Belén. El Barcelona volverá a jugar el jueves como local, esta vez en el Camp Nou, el jueves (18:45 horas) ante el Arsenal en la Champions League, cerrando la semana el domingo (18:00 horas) ante el Deportivo en Riazor.

articles.title: Una victoria de 'Primera' para un Almería que ya es primero
articles.standfirst: Los indálicos asaltan Montilivi con un gol de Miguel de la Fuente, que ya suma ocho tantos en Liga
articles.summary: Los indálicos asaltan Montilivi con un gol de Miguel de la Fuente, que ya suma ocho tantos en Liga
articles.body: El Almería asaltó Montilivi con un trabajado triunfo por 0-1 gracias al oportunismo de Miguel de la Fuente, autor del único tanto del encuentro en la segunda mitad, que dedicó su gol en la entrevista postpartido a Jesús de Miguel y su familia. Los de García Pimienta firmaron una actuación muy seria para sumar tres puntos de enorme valor que les permiten situarse como líderes provisionales de LaLiga Hypermotion y prolongar su espectacular racha hasta las 10 jornadas consecutivas sin perder. Girona y Almería comenzaron el encuentro tratando de llevar la iniciativa con el balón, aunque las primeras ocasiones tardaron en llegar para ambos conjuntos. Los de Quique Álvarez estuvieron cerca de inaugurar el marcador diez minutos después del emotivo homenaje que Montilivi brindó a Jesús de Miguel, con un disparo de Abel Ruiz dentro del área que Bonini desvió a saque de esquina con una intervención salvadora. Cipenga respondió para los almerienses en el minuto 32 con un disparo desde la frontal que se marchó rozando el palo corto de la portería defendida por Gazzaniga. Carles Pérez probó a Andrés Fernández con un tiro lejano que supuso el primer disparo entre los tres palos del Girona, aunque el guardameta blocó sin problemas el balón, centrado, justo antes del descanso. La segunda mitad comenzó sin cambios en ninguno de los dos equipos y con una parada prodigiosa de Andrés Fernández sobre la línea de gol a los tres minutos, tras un remate a bocajarro de Abel Ruiz. El Almería, no obstante, no desaprovechó un balón muerto que quedó dentro del área gerundense después de un remate de Luna, y Miguel de la Fuente, el más listo de la clase, se lanzó al suelo con todo para empujar el balón al fondo de la portería de Gazzaniga y poner el 0-1 en el minuto 67. Los indálicos pudieron sentenciar el encuentro en el tramo final con un remate de Baptistao, a centro de Dzodic, que Gazzaniga desvió con una gran intervención. En la continuación de la jugada fue el Girona quien rozó el empate con un disparo de Vanat dentro del área que Lelo desvió in extremis. El conjunto local tuvo la última en la cabeza del gigantón Pyshchur, pero volvió a aparecer Andrés Fernández para salvar al Almería antes de que el delantero reclamara penalti en la continuación de la acción.

articles.title: College football winners and losers: Are teams like LSU, Ole Miss and Ohio State now out of the playoff race?
articles.summary: All three teams lost their third games of the season on Saturday.
articles.body:
Saturday showed exactly why there was no need to overreact to the first set of College Football Playoff rankings.

Week 10 brought us six matchups between teams in the top 20 of the initial rankings. And when you throw in Ohio State's upset loss at home to Oregon, seven teams with legitimate playoff hopes lost this weekend.

And of those seven, only No. 1 Miami can consider its playoff hopes still relatively safe.

The other six teams that didn't win all suffered either their second or third defeats. It's highly likely that a 9-3 team or two will make the final 12-team playoff at the end of the season. But for the four contenders that just suffered their third loss, their wiggle room is gone with three weeks to go in the regular season. Don't be surprised if just one or two of the teams listed below end up having a chance to play for the national title.

Games remaining: at No. 2 Georgia, vs. No. 6 Kentucky, vs. Oklahoma

Saturday's result: Lost 34-20 to No. 7 Texas

We'll start with a team that we think has the smallest chance of getting to the playoff of any of the top-20 teams who lost on Saturday.

The Tigers were almost certainly a playoff team at 10-2 and can still make the playoff at 9-3. But the odds of Missouri heading to Georgia and beating the Bulldogs are very slim, especially after the way the Tigers failed to capitalize in that loss to Texas. Yes, a lot of close replays went against Mizzou. But the Tigers also missed two field goals and had a grand total of 16 yards on their four drives after Texas tied the game at 20-20.

Games remaining : vs. No. 7 Texas, at No. 13 Tennessee, at Arkansas

Saturday's result: Lost 31-13 to No. 5 Alabama

Do you trust these Tigers to win their remaining three games? A win over Alabama would have allowed LSU to likely be in the playoff with a split of the games against UT-abbreviated teams and a win over Arkansas. Now, LSU needs to beat both Texas and Tennessee. Those wins could be enough to get LSU into the playoff at 9-3.

But if those games are losses? LSU is staring at a 7-5 campaign. And that's hardly what anyone had in mind after the school and the state lured Lane Kiffin to Baton Rouge.

Games remaining: vs. Northwestern, at Nebraska, vs. Michigan

Saturday's result: Lost 41-28 to No. 23 Oregon

Ohio State will be favored to win each of its next three games. But Ohio State is going to need a ton of help to make the playoff at 9-3. While the three-loss SEC teams in the vicinity of Ohio State have ranked opponents remaining on their schedules, the Buckeyes don't. The best case for Ohio State is that it wins out and teams like Ole Miss, LSU and Missouri lose a fourth game and others falter too. But that may be asking too much. For the first time in the 12-team playoff era, Ohio State looks like it'll be on the outside looking in.

Games remaining: at Oklahoma, vs. Wofford, vs. Mississippi State

How far are the Rebels going to drop on Tuesday? It'd be a lot easier to feel confident about Ole Miss' playoff chances if what unfolded at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium wasn't a butt-kicking. Instead, the Rebels got absolutely blown out by No. 2 Georgia and could end up falling outside the top 15.

And if that happens, Ole Miss is staring at the same question Ohio State is. What's the path back into the playoff without any games against ranked teams remaining? Ole Miss' playoff case could get even weaker if LSU loses to both Texas and Tennessee. Rebels fans, prepare to root for LSU to win at least one of those games. The strength of that head-to-head win may prove paramount.

Games remaining: vs. Baylor, at Kansas, vs. Cincinnati

Saturday's result: Lost 28-20 to No. 3 Utah

The Cougars did a great job of bouncing back from Utah's opening salvos and taking the lead in the first half. But ultimately, four turnovers were hard to overcome as the No. 3 Utes won the Holy War to stay undefeated.

BYU's win over Notre Dame got a huge boost thanks to the Irish's victory over Miami. And the host of three-loss teams below the Cougars in the playoffs rankings are a boon as well. The worst-case scenario for BYU as it stands right now is that Texas Tech beats Utah in the Big 12 title game and the CFP committee fills the field without a third Big 12 team.

Games remaining: vs. No. 24 Florida, at No. 18 Missouri, vs. Louisville

The Wildcats made a living winning games on the margins through the first nine weeks of the season. That all came crashing down against Tennessee. Kentucky turned the ball over three times and failed to score a touchdown against a Tennessee team that should move into the top 10 on Tuesday.

Kentucky is probably still in good shape for the playoff at 10-2. But can it get in at 9-3? We're not so sure. LSU is the Wildcats' signature win and it came by a point in overtime.

Here are the rest of this week's winners and losers.

Florida Atlantic: The Owls threw a wrench into the American title game race on Thursday night with a 60-29 drubbing of UTSA. WR Easton Messer continued his tear with seven catches for 85 yards and three scores, and the Owls rushed for 339 yards on just 49 attempts. UTSA entered Week 10 undefeated in conference play and a favorite to make the title game. Now, the Roadrunners could face a must-win against North Texas on Nov. 14.

Tulsa: It might be an understatement to call Tulsa's win over Tulane a dominant one. The Golden Hurricane went to New Orleans and scored the first 46 points in a 60-10 rout. QB Baylor Hayes was 26-of-33 passing for 338 yards and four touchdowns. Three of them went to Oran Singleton Jr., who had 13 catches for 177 yards and three scores. Four different Tulsa players scored rushing touchdowns, too.

The win puts Tulsa at 5-4 overall and a win away from the school's first bowl game since 2021. And it also forced Tulane athletic director David Harris to issue a statement after the game.

"Today's performance by our football program was unacceptable, and far below the standard that we have come to expect in recent years," Harris said. "I understand the frustration and disappointment that our supporters feel. I am embarrassed by what transpired on the field in front of our student-athletes' families, alumni, fans and the entire Tulane community. While any loss is difficult to accept, today's defeat was particularly alarming given the point differential. Our play was not representative of the work, discipline and sacrifice made by those who established the standard we expect from Tulane Football."

Duke: The Blue Devils absolutely have to be ranked on Tuesday night. Duke moved to 7-2 with a 41-3 win over NC State that included a 109-yard kick-6 by safety Andrew Pellicciotta late in the first half. Star RB Nate Sheppard continued his run through the ACC with 217 yards and three scores on just 18 carries. The Duke defense held NC State to 217 yards on 63 plays as the Wolfpack had just 12 first downs to Duke's 26.

Baylor: The Bears are in the midst of the interim coach bounce and are officially heading to a bowl game. Baylor improved to 6-3 overall with a 42-31 home win over Iowa State as QB DJ Lagway had three total touchdowns. The school fired Dave Aranda after a loss to Kansas and has now won two straight since Joe Klanderman took over as the team's interim for the rest of the season. Those might end up being key wins, too. Baylor plays BYU, Texas Tech and Houston to end the season.

Florida State: That interim coach bounce also applies to Florida State. The Seminoles won their first road game since their undefeated 2023 regular season in a 31-24 win at Boston College. The game was FSU's first since firing Mike Norvell after Week 9 and the first victory for interim coach Rick Stockstill since the penultimate weekend of the 2023 season when he was the coach at Middle Tennessee. Amari Thomas had 19 carries for 98 yards and two scores and the defense came up with two interceptions.

Michigan: Things are getting worse in Ann Arbor. The Wolverines lost 15-6 at home to Michigan State on Saturday night. The Spartans entered the game winless in the Big Ten.

The Wolverines had just 192 yards of offense on 52 plays as QB Tommy Carr threw two interceptions. Michigan was in real danger of getting shut out at home for the first time since 1967 — also a loss to Michigan State — before scoring a touchdown with 1:35 to go.

The loss drops Michigan to 5-4 overall ahead of games against No. 23 Oregon, No. 8 UCLA and No. 12 Ohio State. There's a very real chance Michigan could end the season at 5-7.

Nebraska: All the promise that Nebraska's 5-0 start brought Husker fans has quickly disappeared. Nebraska dropped to 5-4 overall with a 24-13 loss at Illinois on Friday night. Nebraska has scored 17 or fewer points in all four of those losses, and coach Matt Rhule fired offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen on Saturday.

How much will the offensive coordinator change matter? This is Rhule's fourth season at Nebraska and the Huskers have gone 7-6 in each of the previous two seasons. In 2024, Nebraska lost four straight after starting the season 5-1. A season ago, Nebraska lost three straight at the end of the season and five of its final seven games after starting 5-1. If you're sensing a pattern, you're not alone.

TCU: The Horned Frogs dropped to 4-5 with an incredibly brutal loss to Arizona late Friday night as they allowed the Wildcats to score twice inside the final two minutes for a 29-28 win. TCU went up eight with 6:35 to go and Arizona had the chance to tie the game with a 2-point conversion after scoring with 1:45 remaining.

That conversion failed. Arizona then tried a pooch kick on the kickoff and, well, TCU failed to recover it.

Four plays later, Michael Salgado-Medina buried a 37-yard field goal for the game-winning points.

Kansas State: Collin Klein's first season in charge of the Wildcats is in the middle of a slide. Kansas State lost its third straight game and fell to 1-5 in the Big 12 with a 66-28 home loss to Oklahoma State. The Cowboys scored seven touchdowns in the first half despite two turnovers by Drew Mestemaker. That's how badly things went for K-State.

Mestemaker ended up throwing for four scores, rushing for one and catching another. Kansas State QBs Blake Barnett and Dillon Duff combined to throw three interceptions, as the Wildcats have struggled in starting QB Avery Johnson's absence.

Kansas: It was not a great day in the Sunflower State. A familiar script unfolded for Kansas fans. The Jayhawks turned a 26-14 deficit into a 32-26 lead over UCF with 1:06 to go with a Dylan Edwards touchdown. But like has happened so often in recent years, the Jayhawks couldn't hold the lead. UCF went 73 yards in 10 plays as Caden Piening made a 6-yard TD catch with a second to go for a 33-32 win.

It's the first road win for the Knights since the 2024 season and puts UCF just a win away from a bowl game. Kansas, meanwhile, is tied at the bottom of the Big 12 with its in-state rival — and loses the head-to-head tiebreaker — as it needs to win out to get to 6-6.

articles.title: Maffeo se disculpa tras su polémica entrevista al descanso ante el Real Madrid: "Estaba muy caliente"
articles.standfirst: El lateral del Valencia asegura que nunca tuvo intención de faltar al respeto al periodista de DAZN y explica que accedió por ser "obligatoria"
articles.summary: El lateral del Valencia asegura que nunca tuvo intención de faltar al respeto al periodista de DAZN y explica que accedió por ser "obligatoria"
articles.body: El jugador Pablo Maffeo se disculpó este domingo a través de sus redes sociales en las que explicó lo ocurrido durante el descanso del encuentro entre el Valencia y el Real Madrid, después de la polémica generada por sus declaraciones en la entrevista a pie de campo de DAZN. El lateral valencianista publicó una historia en Instagram en la que pidió perdón "si alguien se ha tomado mi reacción como algo personal" y explicó que desde el primer momento manifestó su deseo de no realizar la entrevista porque se encontraba "muy caliente" por las circunstancias del partido. Según relató, le comunicaron que la comparecencia era "obligatoria" y acabó accediendo a realizarla. Durante la entrevista al descanso, con el Valencia perdiendo por 0-2, Maffeo mostró abiertamente su malestar y aseguró que no le apetecía atender a los medios: "No me apetece nada hacer esta entrevista, es una mierda esta entrevista aquí, que no pinta nada, estamos jugando un partido", dijo inicialmente el jugador sin escuchar la pregunta que se le había formulado. Además, cuestionó varias decisiones arbitrales, especialmente la falta señalada sobre Kylian Mbappé en la acción previa al primer gol madridista, en la que el futbolista del Valencia vio tarjeta amarilla. En su mensaje en Instagram, el jugador insistió en que sus palabras no iban dirigidas contra el periodista de DAZN. "Tengo muchísimo respeto por todos los profesionales que hacen su trabajo y él no tiene ninguna culpa de lo sucedido", escribió. Además, explicó que al término del encuentro se acercó personalmente al reportero para aclararle que su reacción no debía interpretarse como algo personal. Las cámaras de la plataforma captaron esa conversación -sin audio, con una cámara lejana- una vez finalizado el partido, en la que Maffeo trasladó sus disculpas al periodista Sergio Quirante, tal y como posteriormente señaló el propio periodista durante la retransmisión. En la parte final de su comunicado, el futbolista afirma que su único objetivo era "aclarar cómo ocurrieron las cosas" y dejar constancia de que "nunca hubo intención de faltar al respeto a nadie".

articles.title: Óskarsson no defrauda y derrota al Rayo
articles.standfirst: La Real superó en Anoeta al Rayo en un partido con alternativas, pudiendo los txuriurdin vencer con algo menos de sufrimiento, pero los vallecanos también empatar
articles.summary: La Real superó en Anoeta al Rayo en un partido con alternativas, pudiendo los txuriurdin vencer con algo menos de sufrimiento, pero los vallecanos también empatar
articles.body: Orri Óskarsson apuntaba a ser un futbolista muy importante para la Real Sociedad, porque llevaba una racha de cuatro goles en cinco partidos, y más aún por la baja de Mikel Oyarzabal, y el conjunto txuriurdin se agarró al islandés para derrotar a un Rayo Vallecano que tuvo opciones para empatar. Óskarsson pudo marcar ya a los 20 segundos, pero su remate solo ante Audero, aunque un poco escorado eso sí, se fue desviado. El ariete islandés pidió penalti apenas un par de minutos después, pero no lo pareció y Munuera Montero y el VAR tampoco lo vieron. El Rayo contestó con un zurdazo lejano de Tsitaishvili a las manos de Remiro, con el de nuevo internacional Barrenetxea disparando ligeramente alto, ya con un juego más igualado. Tras unos minutos sin acciones destacables, Turrientes realizó una individual de calidad, pero su pase de la muerte no encontró rematador, tampoco el que hizo Kubo prácticamente idéntico. Sucic probó desde lejos, pero la pelota salió alta, yéndose al lateral de la red la del disparo de un insistente japonés. El croata también lo volvió a intentar, pero la pelota se fue desviada por unos centímetros. Parecía que el choque era totalmente txuriurdin, pero Unai le puso un pase milimétrico a De Frutos, cuyo empalme se fue arriba de la meta local. Un cabezazo sin buena dirección de Jon Martín fue lo último antes del descanso Real y Rayo llegaron pronto a área nada más volver de los vestuarios, pero con fueras de juego de Camello y Kubo. Los de Matarazzo enseguida inclinaron el campo a su favor, con varios córners seguidos y un cabezazo flojo y centrado de Turrientes a las manos de Audero. Mucho más difícil fue la que sacó Remiro, ante una volea potente de De Frutos, para evitar que los visitantes se pusieran por sorpresa por delante. El técnico realista fue el primero en mover el banquillo, con las entradas de Fort y Guedes, pero Pedro Díaz falló lo infallable en boca de gol. Del susto, Remiro inició una contra al pasarle a Barrenetxea, que dejó solo a Óskarsson ante Audero, poniendo el islandés el 1-0. Sadick estuvo a punto de empatar en un córner y Lejeune buscó hacerlo de una falta de las suyas, pero se topó con otra manopla de Remiro. Ochieng y Guedes tuvieron, sobre todo el primero, dos buenísimas opciones para sentenciar, pero no lo hicieron y casi lo pagan, porque Isi rozó el empate, pero su balón se fue al palo, en la última del partido.

articles.title: FAI Cup final: First Derry City goal worth the wait for cup final hero Darragh Burns
articles.summary: Derry City's FAI Cup final hero Darragh Burns says there is "nowhere better" to get his first goal for the club than scoring the winner at the Aviva Stadium in the decider.
articles.body:
Derry City's FAI Cup hero Darragh Burns said there is "nowhere better" to get his first goal for the club than at the Aviva Stadium in a final.

Burns' low drive on 69 minutes broke the deadlock for the Candystripes against a spirited Waterford and was enough to secure the club's seventh FAI Cup victory.

The 24-year-old was set to be substituted before he fired home and was relieved to contribute with his first goal since arriving at the club in July.

"I saw the substitutions getting going and I said to myself 'please just produce something' and it went in the back of the net so I'm over the moon," he told BBC Sport NI's Odhran Crumley.

"It took me longer than I expected to score my first goal, but nowhere better to get it than at the Aviva in the cup final. I dreamt of it last night and it's come true today.

"I hadn't had a shot yet in the game, just checked in on left, fake shot, went again and it hit the net.

"It's been a difficult year for the club, but we would have taken your hand off for this at the start of the season, so delighted."

Derry City secure FAI Cup with narrow Waterford win

'Best feeling in football' for captain Duffy

Candystripes captain Michael Duffy has now won the FAI Cup five times, twice with Dundalk and three times with his hometown club but said this latest triumph was his best moment in football.

He added that captaining Derry to silverware for the first time left him "lost for words" at the final whistle.

"That tops it off for me, it's the best feeling I've had in football," he said.

"The final whistle got me big time, I didn't know what to do or where to go. Just so, so happy getting my hands on that trophy. I've been thinking about it for the last week to be honest, so unbelievable feeling, something I'll never forget."

While acknowledging that Derry, who finished fifth in the Premier Division after a tumultuous campaign that saw manager Tiernan Lynch depart in August, "weren't good enough" in the first six months of the season, Duffy was delighted they regrouped and finished on a high with a trophy that also brings qualification for the Europa League in 2027-28.

"Mark [Connolly] has been brilliant for us and we knew we could make this happen and we went and done that. We go into next year on a massive high," he added.

"I didn't even think about that [Europa League] but it's another plus and the club is going in the right direction with a lot of exciting things."

articles.title: Beñat San José: "Nos duele irnos de vacío"
articles.standfirst: El técnico vasco analizó la derrota del Rayo ante la Real Sociedad
articles.summary: El técnico vasco analizó la derrota del Rayo ante la Real Sociedad
articles.body: Beñat San José se fue "frustrado" de su casa. El guipuzcoano volvió a Anoeta, esta vez como entrenador del Rayo Vallecano, y lamentó en rueda de prensa las ocasiones que desperdició su equipo. También habló sobre el ambiente en el campo, el trabajo en la finalización y el cambio de Vetrouwd. Derrota: "Estamos muy fastidiados. Mucho dolor. No la merecíamos. La primera parte ha sido de tú a tú, tampoco nos han hecho mucho daño. Ellos han tenido algunos ataques peligrosos y nosotros unos cuantos muy buenos. Hemos podido sacar más. En la segunda parte, cuando mejor estábamos, nos ha venido un fatídico gol que viene de un córner nuestro. Nos duele irnos de vacío. Hoy se nos ha negado el gol. Nos merecíamos mínimamente el empate". Público desplazado: "Es muy especial. Lástima que está esa mampara, que no se les ha podido oir muy bien. Nos da mucha energía. En esta visita las dos aficiones se llevan bien y da gusto. Ha habido un ambiente muy bueno". Vuelta a Anoeta: "Una vez que empieza el partido, uno se mete de lleno para conseguir la victoria para su equipo. Pero es un momento tremendamente especial. La Real es mi casa. Me crió como jugador, entrenador y hay personas maravillosas dentro del club que hacen un trabajo extraordinario". Finalización: "El juego ofensivo lo practicamos mucho, tenemos gente con virtud. La última finalización se practica continuamente y el previo pase también lo tenemos que seguir trabajando". Cambio de Jozhua en apenas 10 minutos: "Ha sido un cambio por problemas físicos porque él lo ha pedido. No sé al detalle, ahora me dirá el doctor. Se ha quedado clavado en una acción bastante fuerte. Lo hemos tenido que cambiar forzadamente".

articles.title: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea: Xabi Alonso tinkers again as Blues lose to Black Cats
articles.summary: Xabi Alonso's frustration is evident as Chelsea's struggles for an identity continue with the disappointing 1-0 defeat by Sunderland.
articles.body:
Constant changes in formation and personnel - and another disappointing defeat.

Xabi Alonso's frustration was obvious as Chelsea 's struggles for identity continued in the 1-0 defeat by Sunderland .

It is starting to feel as though the Spaniard is the latest "Tinkerman" at Stamford Bridge, a moniker first associated with Blues boss Claudio Ranieri back in 2002-03.

For the first time this season, Chelsea lined up with a three-man midfield - but they were also without a recognised striker for the second match in a row, with Pedro Neto again struggling to lead the line in their loss at the Stadium of Light.

By contrast, struggling Sunderland were led by target man Brian Brobbey, who won a 36th-minute penalty after being brought down by Levi Colwill. Enzo le Fee converted the game's only goal from the spot.

That decision came moments after Chelsea were denied a penalty when Cole Palmer went down under a challenge from Luke O'Nien, but the video assistant referee ruled that contact had started outside the box.

Those two incidents in quick succession meant Alonso and his coaching staff appeared angry on the touchline after the Sunderland goal.

However, the Chelsea manager refused to criticise the officials after the game - instead he gave brief answers that changed the subject and were critical towards his players for not carrying out the gameplan properly.

Asked whether Brobbey was simply unstoppable, Alonso, 44, replied: "No, he's stoppable. He's stoppable, but we have to do it better than we did today.

"Out of almost nothing he got a couple of chances. He got the penalty as well.

"I'm not happy with how we defended that situation. It's something that we could have avoided, something that we had worked on during the week. To concede penalties is not good for us."

It left nowhere to hide for Colwill, who was substituted at half-time, with Moises Caicedo filling in at centre-back despite having barely completed a full training session all week and needing careful management of his own fitness issues.

Chelsea also created few clear chances, aside from a headed opportunity that £117m signing Morgan Rogers squandered, while Palmer also struggled - days after being left out of the England squad.

Before the season started, Alonso said he wanted his Chelsea side to be "unpredictable".

Although factors such as injuries are beyond his control, his side have achieved that, but to their own detriment.

Failed to deal with Brobbey - player ratings for Sunderland v Chelsea

Sunderland beat Chelsea for first league win since August

Only Tottenham (28) have made more more line-up changes than Chelsea (24) in the Premier League this season.

In the early part of the campaign, they at least had a settled and exciting front three of Joao Pedro, Rogers and Palmer.

It was largely the reason behind the positive start to the season despite failing to keep a clean sheet against top-flight opposition until Alonso's eighth game in charge.

With Caicedo injured, they suffered problems in midfield and continued to make changes from match to match, while also experimenting with personnel to fix the defence.

However, they largely looked on course to emulate the back-three system Alonso excelled with during his historic German double-winning season at Bayer Leverkusen in 2023-24.

As Caicedo returned after the international break, however, captain Reece James was injured.

Joao Pedro featured in wins against Bournemouth and Everton before sustaining a thigh injury, having already missed Brazil's international matches.

Number one goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez broke his jaw in a collision at Everton , while Maxence Lacroix, who had been a near ever-present since joining from Crystal Palace in the summer, is expected to be out until January with a hamstring injury.

Defender Jorrel Hato has also suffered a setback in recent weeks.

It has left Alonso reacting to events when selecting his starting XI, with the Spaniard saying: "There are situations. Yesterday Josh [Acheampong] said he was not ready to play, so we are short of options and we need to walk through this step.

"Even when we win, when we lose, we miss some players that we have injured and for sure we are waiting for them to come back because they are important."

He admitted his side were missing Joao Pedro, although supporters have also been frustrated that Estevao Willian, who came on at half-time on Sunday, has started only one league match this season.

Prior to Sunday's game, Chelsea were averaging just 46% possession. They then dominated the ball at Sunderland (with 68.7% possession) but without creating many significant chances.

Meanwhile, only Crystal Palace have conceded more shots on target than Chelsea 's 50, while the Blues top the league with 53 shots on target - meaning there have been plenty of chances at both ends during their matches.

Alonso can still be pleased with Chelsea having collected five more points than they managed from the equivalent fixtures last season, with the club on course to qualify for the Champions League while sitting fifth in the table.

However, that is a low bar after a dismal campaign last season, when Chelsea finished 10th.

Going into the November international break, Alonso remains a long way from establishing a style of play, or an identity capable of bringing consistency - although he promised promising in an interview last week that Chelsea would be "different" and "better" by the end of the season.

articles.title: La dura queja de Lucas González en Nacional por la Selección: A Montero sí lo dejan y a los nuestros no"
articles.standfirst: Lucas González estalla contra las convocatorias de la Selección
articles.summary: Lucas González estalla contra las convocatorias de la Selección
articles.body: Lucas González, técnico de Atlético Nacional, criticó la falta de “coherencia” en las convocatorias de la Selección Colombia tras perder a Samuel Velásquez y Juan Manuel Rengifo justo antes de una semifinal decisiva de la Copa BetPlay. Su reclamo se centra en que, mientras jugadores de clubes colombianos deben presentarse a la Selección bajo amenaza de sanción, Álvaro Montero pudo permanecer en Boca Juniors para disputar una semifinal de la Copa Argentina. La molestia de González surgió después de la victoria 4-3 de Atlético Nacional sobre Deportivo Pereira, un partido en el que el equipo verdolaga tuvo que remontar sobre el final y en el que el entrenador reconoció graves fallas defensivas. Aunque el resultado fue positivo, el DT calificó el desempeño como “el peor partido” de su etapa al frente del club. La preocupación inmediata no era solo el rendimiento, sino el calendario: Nacional deberá afrontar la semifinal de la Copa BetPlay ante Once Caldas y, además, la última fecha del todos contra todos de la Liga BetPlay. En ese contexto, la pérdida de piezas importantes por convocatorias internacionales representa un golpe deportivo directo. Néstor Lorenzo incluyó a Samuel Velásquez y Juan Manuel Rengifo en la lista de 26 convocados de la Selección Colombia de mayores para los amistosos ante Chile, programados para el 13 y 17 de noviembre. Ambos ya habían integrado el proceso en la fecha anterior, y Velásquez incluso marcó un gol en la victoria 2-0 sobre Perú. La situación se agrava porque Nacional también cede jugadores a las selecciones juveniles: Felipe Marín y Jhoan Quesada fueron llamados a la Sub-19, mientras que Cristian Arboleda, Edwin Echevarría, Juan Carlos Moreno, José Escorcia, Nicolás Bernal y Simón Rojas integraron la convocatoria de la Sub-17. En total, González calculó que el club perdería entre ocho y nueve futbolistas del primer equipo durante la fecha FIFA. El núcleo del reclamo de González es la comparación con Álvaro Montero, arquero colombiano que milita en Boca Juniors. Montero no fue convocado para los amistosos ante Chile y, según el técnico de Nacional, se quedó en Argentina para jugar la semifinal de la Copa Argentina con su club. Para González, la diferencia es evidente: mientras un jugador de un club colombiano debe acudir a la Selección o exponer a su institución a una sanción, Montero pudo priorizar un compromiso decisivo con Boca. “Álvaro Montero, por ejemplo, él se queda para jugar la semifinal de Copa en Argentina, pero los jugadores nuestros sí tienen que ir, porque si no el club es sancionado”, afirmó el entrenador. La convocatoria confirma que Montero no apareció en la lista de Lorenzo; en su lugar fue llamado Devis Vásquez, del AS Roma. Esto refuerza la percepción de González de que existen criterios distintos según el club, la liga o la situación competitiva del jugador.

articles.title: Matarazzo: "Ganar sufriendo también forma parte del fútbol"
articles.standfirst: El técnico realista valoró la portería a cero, pero más el superar a un equipo como el Rayo
articles.summary: El técnico realista valoró la portería a cero, pero más el superar a un equipo como el Rayo
articles.body: Pellegrino Matarazzo se mostró muy satisfecho con la victoria de la Real Sociedad, porque destacó el gran nivel del Rayo y el lograrla en una semana con tres partidos muy duros. El técnico valoró la portería a cero, pero más los tres puntos. Matarazzo valoró así el partido. “No ha sido un partido fácil hoy. Pienso que empezamos muy bien el encuentro y tuvimos una buena primera parte, en la que creamos muchas ocasiones y oportunidades, como para habernos puesto en ventaja. Creo que Orri y Ander tuvieron las dos mejores ocasiones de la mitad al inicio, y también tuvimos jugadas de peligro que cruzaron el área con un remate muy claro que no logramos materializar en el 1-0. El segundo tiempo fue muy igualado, muy abierto, el Rayo tuvo su ocasión, pero luego marcamos nosotros y ganamos. ¿Sufriendo? Sufrir también forma parte del fútbol”. Se le destacó la portería a cero. “Estoy más contento por los tres puntos. A veces no es fácil crear ocasiones, ya vimos contra el Lyon que tuvimos dificultades con espacios más reducidos, hoy fue parecido. Cuando el juego ofensivo no fluye tanto, necesitas defender bien y conceder muy pocas ocasiones, y hoy pienso que hoy lo hicimos; concedimos alguna ocasión en la segunda mitad, pero defendimos como equipo al igual que hicimos contra el Lyon, estoy muy contento con el rendimiento defensivo en los últimos dos partidos”. Matarazzo lamentó la lesión de Barrenetxea. “Todo indica que sufre una lesión muscular, aunque todavía no sabemos con exactitud la gravedad, hay que esperar a hacerle pruebas médicas para comprobarlo. Es muy desafortunado porque ‘Barrene’ se encontraba en un momento excelente y estaba realizando un gran partido hoy. Es un jugador muy importante para nosotros en los últimos partidos, pero volverá y regresará con más fuerza, estoy seguro”.

articles.title: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa: Patrick Dorgu levels in the 96th minute as United come from two down TWICE to earn incredible draw
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Manchester United score twice in stoppage-time in a wild 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford. Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu help Michael Carrick's men come from two down again but United still in relegation zone
articles.body:
Under-pressure boss Michael Carrick saw his side go 2-0 down inside four minutes but they fought back to level before half-time only to disintegrate defensively again early in the second half. Many had departed when they launched their latest improbable comeback.

Joshua Zirkzee swept in what looked like a consolation goal in the 92nd minute and when Zion Suzuki flapped at one final corner, Patrick Dorgu headed into the net to stun Villa. United still have not won a Premier League game since August but it was Unai Emery fuming.

Villa were rampant at the start, Alysson beating Senne Lammens on the angle inside a minute before the same player's shot proved too hot for the goalkeeper to handle and presented Nicolas Jackson with the chance to put United two down after four minutes.

That was the earliest that United had been two down in a Premier League game but Old Trafford only had to look to Tuesday - and their 3-2 victory over Roma - to recognise that being two behind need not be fatal to their hopes. Momentum did turn in their favour.

Matheus Cunha drew a penalty when Boubacar Kamara lunged in and Bruno Fernandes converted. Suzuki's goal was peppered thereafter, the chants from the Stretford End against the ownership briefly subsiding as United pushed for a deserved equaliser.

Youri Tielemans found it against his former club before the interval and United looked narrow favourites at the break. But another calamitous start to a half undermined them, Diogo Dalot bringing down Alysson for John McGinn to score from the penalty spot.

When Leny Yoro headed towards his own goal soon after and Lammens could only push it against the post, Jackson miskicked before Leon Goretzka forced the ball home to restore Villa's two-goal advantage. United's lamentable defending is a massive issue.

At that stage, there could be no confidence that a defence that has now conceded more goals than any other in Europe's major leagues in all competitions would not let in a fifth but, instead of it petering out, Zirkzee and Dorgu came off the bench to do the unthinkable.

The point still lifts Villa into the top half of the table but feels like two dropped. As for United - this chaotic, confusing United - they are in the relegation zone after 10 games. A club at odds with its fans, running on fumes, but still capable of two comebacks in one game.

Carrick bemoans 'totally avoidable' goals

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick speaking in the press conference:

"We kind of beat ourselves a little bit with the moments really that we're giving away and goals that we're giving away in tight clusters that are making it a lot more difficult. It's hard enough anyway, but making it a lot more difficult than it should be.

"Football is about moments, football is about what happens in both boxes in the end, but I think you take [out] the moments that are totally avoidable goals that we're giving away, I actually thought we played pretty well and were the better team for the most part, and I'm disappointed that we still haven't won the game, to be truthful.

"I thought we had most of the pressure. I thought we defended well, pressed well. We just gave them the moments that shape the game in some ways, and then finished strongly and took something out of the game, but still disappointment that we haven't actually won it."

Asked if there are positives to take into the international break:

"Yeah, 100 per cent, yeah. I think there's more than enough. Goals change games and you've got to deal with it, and it's part of something we have to improve on drastically, but there's more than enough. We're just making it too difficult for ourselves at the moment in certain times."

Asked if he is expecting talks over his future:

I'm quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it's got to win games."

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery speaking in the press conference:

"Angry, of course. To accept to lose in the last minutes two goals, it is difficult.

"I am angry for the situation, not with the players. We lost the opportunity to have two points more."

Asked about how Aston Villa allowed Manchester United to come back:

"They did the same here against Roma with the supporters pushing, they were playing with heart. The last moments when we were close to finishing the match, with Dorgu left side, we couldn't defend him good."

Asked if he thinks Manchester United are better than the Premier League table suggests:

"Yes, definitely. The Premier League is very difficult. You must be so, so demanding but they have the capacity, powerful players to overcome this situation.

"Of course, there are other teams performing fantastic. Last year, Tottenham and West Ham, important teams [were down there]. The year before United when they played the final of the Europa League.

"It is very demanding. You must compete, be strong, give them confidence to play with their quality. A lot of things. But of course normally Manchester United are going to improve."

Former Man Utd captain Roy Keane speaking on Sky Sports:

"There have been question marks over this team showing a bit of fight, a bit of desire. And as bad as the game was from a football point of view they kept going until the end.

"They kept going, so you have to give them a little bit of praise.

"But in terms of the bigger picture it's that rollercoaster of watching United. Some bits were so, so bad. Defensively, the start to the first half, the start to the second half, but they found a way to get a point when they looked dead and buried. Ultimately nowhere near good enough to try to get towards the middle of the table.

"They're probably lacking a bit of confidence but if you're giving up four goals at home, you make it so hard for yourself. When they were on a good run of results last year, the goalkeeper was doing very well, making a lot of big saves, he's not doing that. Bruno was on fire, he's not at his very best at the moment.

"There are some basic footballing reasons... but to be in the bottom three, playing for Man Utd, is rightly so - and should be - hurting them."

articles.title: Un 'milagro' del Manchester United... que no les libra de caer a los infiernos
articles.standfirst: Los 'red devils' igualaron hasta en dos ocasiones ante el Aston Villa de Emery... pero se van al parón en puestos de descenso
articles.summary: Los 'red devils' igualaron hasta en dos ocasiones ante el Aston Villa de Emery... pero se van al parón en puestos de descenso
articles.body: Todavía queda algo de lo que un día se conocía como 'El Teatro de los Sueños'. El Manchester United, que venía de firmar una remontada épica contra la Roma, logró marcar dos goles en el tiempo de descuento para terminar empatando un encuentro absolutamente 'loco' contra el Aston Villa de Unai Emery (4-4). Un 'milagro' que, sin embargo, no fue suficiente para evitar caer a los puestos de descenso. Su trascendental actuación contra la Roma devolvió a Matheus Cunha al once de un Manchester United donde Yoro formó pareja con Maguire, mientras que Mainoo y Tielemans fueron los encargados de llevar la 'manija'. Emery, por su parte, sorprendió haciendo debutar en Premier a un Harwood-Bellis que, unos metros por delante, tenía a Alysson como socio. Goretzka, por su parte, fue el socio de Kamara en la medular. La apuesta por el joven extremo brasileño le salió a pedir de boca al técnico de Hondarribia. Y es que, cuando apenas había transcurrido un minuto de partido, fue el encargado de poner en ventaja al Aston Villa definiendo al primer toque desde el área pequeña en el lado débil... culminando una jugada que nació en un saque de banda. Fue, desde luego, un golpe directo al mentón de un Manchester United que, antes de llegar al minuto cinco, ya estaba contra las cuerdas. De nuevo, Alysson sacó su disparo a pasear, Lammens dejó el rechace suelto y Nico Jackson estuvo rápido para duplicar la ventaja. Noveno gol del senegalés, que ha renacido con Emery. No había hecho nada más que comenzar el encuentro y el Manchester United ya se estaba desangrando. Antes de cumplirse el primer cuarto de hora, sin embargo, Matheus Cunha se rebeló y acabó sacándole un penalti a Kamara. Asumió la responsabilidad Bruno Fernandes... y no falló. El partido dio un giro radical. El Manchester United recobró fuerzas, se levantó de la lona y comenzó a asediar a Zion Suzuki. Le negó el gol a Cunha, Bruno y Diallo... pero no pudo evitar el empate de Tielemans en el 43'. El ex del Aston Villa se asomó por la frontal del área y, a pase de Mazraoui, batió al guardameta japonés con la zurda. Tan sólo unas posibles molestias podían explicar la sustitución de Maguire al descanso. Heaven entró en su lugar y Dalot, que ya había salido señalado en en el 0-1, cometió un penalti sobre Alysson en el 47'. McGinn, que venía de fallar una pena máxima ante el Fulham, convirtió un lanzamiento inapelable. Otra vez, le tocaba levantarse a un Manchester United que vivió un 'dejá vù' respecto a lo sucedido en el inicio del partido. McGinn botó una falta en zona de tres cuartos que, en su intento por despejar, Yoro mandó al larguero... y Goretzka empujó sobre la línea de gol. Una acción completamente anticompetitiva por parte del central francés. "Vuestro funeral, no el nuestro", podía leerse en una pancarta desplegada en uno de los fondos de Old Trafford. No daba señales de reacción el Manchester United. Sin embargo, ya en el tiempo de descuento, Zirkzee recortó distancias a pase de un Patrick Dorgu que igualó en el 94' a la salida de un córner. Sufrió una barbaridad Suzuki a lo largo de todo el partido en este tipo de acciones. Queda por ver si le vale a Carrick para salvar su puesto durante el parón.

articles.title: Man Utd v Aston Villa player ratings: Patrick Dorgu makes dramatic impact
articles.summary: Man Utd fight back from two goals down twice in 4-4 draw with Aston Villa - but who did well and who didn't in player ratings?
articles.body:
Manchester United fought back from two goals twice to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa as Patrick Dorgu made a dramatic impact off the bench.

But who impressed and who didn't in the Old Trafford epic?

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Senne Lammens: One of Man Utd's best performers this season but a calamitous start to this one. First goal went straight through him and he spilled a shot straight from Nicolas Jackson for the second. Went wrong way for penalty too. 4

Diogo Dalot (off 66, Dorgu): Got his body in the right position to close half the goal off for the opener but was in the wrong position to make challenge on Alysson at start of second half to gift Villa a penalty. 4

Leny Yoro: Moved back into the centre, intelligently stepped up to win the ball on halfway, then spoiled good work by attempting a lofted pass when Matheus Cunha wanted it on the ground. Almost headed into his own net in build-up to Villa's fourth goal. 5

Harry Maguire (off 46, Heaven): Managed to clear his head quickly enough to lead United's defence after their shocking start. A doubt pre-match, he went off at half-time. 5

Noussair Mazraoui: Struggled along with many others this season. Asked to push forward, which he seems to find easier for his country but not his club. 4

Youri Tielemans (off 66, Mount): Baited by the Aston Villa fans given his £35m summer move from them, but answered in the best way by driving home an equaliser for his first United goal. 6

Kobbie Mainoo: Threatened with a long-range effort and nearly picked out Amad Diallo's run with a precise chipped pass over the visitors defence. 6

Amad Diallo (off 66, Lacey): Kept his place ahead of crowd favourite Shea Lacey but one chase back into his own box showed why, defensively, it made sense. Came close to an equaliser and should have ended an 11-month wait for a goal but Zion Suzuki saved well. 6

Bruno Fernandes: For the second game running, he kept his cool to covert from the spot when the pressure was at its highest. Looked unhappy at the end despite the comeback. 7

Matheus Cunha: Driving run into the visiting box brought a crucial penalty. Curling effort was heading for the corner but turned around post by Suzuki. United's most dangerous attacker. 7

Bryan Mbeumo (off 83, Zirkzee): Did a lot of chasing in the first half to try to pressure the Villa defence into mistakes. 6

Ayden Heaven (on 46, Maguire): Booked for late tackle on Alysson after being introduced at break. 6

Mason Mount (on 66, Tielemans): Hit the bar with first time shot but sliced later effort over. 6

Shea Lacey (on 66, Amad): Tried to create. 6

Patrick Dorgu (on 66 Dalot): What an ending as he changed the outcome of the game with an assist and goal. 8

Joshua Zirkzee (on 83, Mbeumo): Scored in stoppage time and goal proved crucial. 6

Subs not used: Darlow, De Ligt, Andrey Santos, J Fletcher.

Bizarre & thrilling theatre as Carrick's Man Utd future still in limbo

Premier League: Man Utd score twice in stoppage time to draw with Villa but stay in drop zone

Zion Suzuki: Kept busy as the hosts hunted an equaliser. One excellent save from Cunha and a couple when he benefited from a kind rebound, but bad error for United's late equaliser. 5

Victor Lindelof: Found himself under a lot of pressure on a ground he knows so well and turned in an accomplished performance. 7

Taylor Harwood-Bellis: Had to remain concentrated and wasn't faultless but emerged with credit in the bank. 6

Pau Torres: Guided a header over as Villa attacked but biggest task was trying to stop Cunha. As it turned out, a stride too late getting out when Tielemans scored. Couldn't keep United out in the end. 6

Ian Maatsen: Testing day, trying to stop Amad attacking and looking to beat Mazraoui at the other end. Was doing well until the late drama. 7

Alysson (off 71, Barkley): Even the Brazilian must have been a little bit surprised his first-minute shot ended up in the net. His shot created the second and came so close to adding another to his tally after being released by Goretzka. Won the penalty at start of second half too. 8

Boubacar Kamara: Ill-advised attempted tackle on Cunha led to penalty that offered the hosts a way back into the game. Struggled to contain the home attack. 7

John McGinn (off 71, Hemmings): Everything looked so good in the opening minutes but then had to try to ensure Villa didn't fall apart as United fought back. Kept his concentration to score from the spot and created panic with a free-kick. 7

Leon Goretzka (off 78, Mbaye): Tried to relieve pressure on Villa defence as the hosts fought back and drove home Villa's fourth on a crazy day. 7

Johan Manzambi (off 78, Gomes): Not the easiest game for the Swiss international to shine given its general chaotic nature. Tried to get control but no real chance of that. 5

Nicolas Jackson (off 86, Madjo): Alert to snaffle home the rebound after Lammens had spilled McGinn's shot. Not the best performance but much effective than in his Chelsea days. 7

George Hemmings (on 71, McGinn): Came on to shore things up but move didn't work. 5

Ross Barkley (on 71, Alysson): Won't remember ending with fondness. 5

Subs not used: Bizot, Mings, Buendia, Cisse.

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: Rob Gronkowski Shows Off Army's New Jerseys for Navy Game, Michael Strahan Narrates Epic Hype Video
articles.summary: Army is going to wear special uniforms honoring the legacy of the Ivy Soldier for its highly anticipated rivalry showdown with Navy, so it was only fitting for a special guest to be the one to show off the new look.
articles.body:
Army is going to wear special uniforms honoring the legacy of the Ivy Soldier for its highly anticipated rivalry showdown with Navy, so it was only fitting for a special guest to be the one to show off the new look.

With members of the armed forces in attendance for Fox NFL Sunday as part of a live audience ahead of Veterans Day on Wednesday, Rob Gronkowski showed off the new jerseys with his signature spike before taking off his helmet to reveal it was him.

Michael Strahan was on stage and also played a role in the reveal.

The New York Giants legend narrated the hype video for the new look:

"Ivy moves with the wind," Strahan said. "Quiet, steady, unassuming. But look closer, and you'll find something much stronger. Strong enough to endure, adaptable enough to overcome and resilient enough to grow where others cannot. These are more than characteristics, these are the qualities of a fighting force. A division known throughout the United States Army as the Ivy Soldiers."

He finishes the video by exclaiming, "Go Army, Beat Navy!"

Navy has won the last two matchups, although Army is 6-4 in the last 10.

This year's game takes place on Dec. 12 and could have bowl implications for the Black Knights in particular following a 5-4 start.

articles.title: El Inter sigue siendo la 'bestia negra' de Fàbregas
articles.summary: Cinco derrotas en cinco partidos. Ese es el balance del Como frente al Inter desde su retorno a la Serie A. Venían crecidos tras endosarle un histórico 1-9 al Lens en Champions. Los de Chivu, sin embargo, cuajaron un encuentro prácticamente perfecto (2-0) para dejarles claro a Fàbregas y los suyos que siguen siendo su 'bestia negra'.
articles.body: Cinco derrotas en cinco partidos. Ese es el balance del Como frente al Inter desde su retorno a la Serie A. Venían crecidos tras endosarle un histórico 1-9 al Lens en Champions. Los de Chivu, sin embargo, cuajaron un encuentro prácticamente perfecto (2-0) para dejarles claro a Fàbregas y los suyos que siguen siendo su 'bestia negra'. Fue sorprendente, como poco, la decisión de Chivu a la hora de dejar a Bisseck y Diouf en el banquillo. Arriba, fue Pío Esposito quien volvió a acompañar a Marcus Thuram ante la baja de Lautaro Martínez. Cesc Fàbregas, por su parte, volvió a hacer cambios bajo palos y, en esta ocasión, Robert Sánchez fue quien se enfundó los guantes. Por lo demás, once de gala con Da Cunha, un día más, arrancando como falso extremo por derecha. El Inter tenía claro que el Como no podía adueñarse del balón y comenzar a atraer presiones. La línea de tres centrales hizo ancho el campo y se apoyaron en Calhanoglu, Barella y Zielinski para llevar a los de Cesc a un terreno donde no se sienten cómodos. El conjunto 'neroazzurri' estaba rondando el 1-0 y lo encontró en el 17'. Spence dobló a Marcus Thuram por derecha y sirvió un envío tenso transformado por Pio Esposito. Cuarto gol para el 'bomber' italiano. Necesitaba la pelota el Como para poder hacer pie en el encuentro. El Inter, sin embargo, estaba mucho más vivo en todos los duelos y, menos de 10' después, logró duplicar la ventaja. En esta ocasión, fue Zielinski quien estiró por izquierda y, tras un deficiente despeje por parte de Álex Valle, Marcus Thuram estuvo atento para mandar a guardar el balón desde el área pequeña. Sexto gol del curso para celebrar su vuelta a la selección francesa. Logró darle la vuelta a la posesión el Como durante el tramo final de la primera parte. Ahora bien, la realidad es que no le hicieron ni cosquillas al Inter, seguramente, más serio de toda la temporada. Tuvo que ajustar Fàbregas al descanso. Ricci ocupó el puesto de Perrone junto a Luis Milla, mientras que Smolcic sentó a Baturina para dibujar una línea de tres atrás con el objetivo de plantearle un 'esquema espejo' al Inter... a pesar de tener el resultado en contra. El Como, sin embargo, pudo seguir pagando la diferencia de intensidad con un Inter que, nada más arrancar la segunda parte, rozó el tercero por medio de Dimarco y Marcus Thuram. Perdieron algo de fuelle los de Chivu. Pero, más allá de un remate de Nico Paz a la cruceta, el conjunto 'lariani' nunca estuvo cerca de meterse en el partido. Triunfo que permite a los 'neroazzurri' reponerse de la derrota en el 'Derby' para quedarse a un punto de la Lazio... que deja a los de Cesc fuera de Champions.

articles.title: AP College Football Poll 2026 Week 11 Rankings Released with Top Risers and Fallers
articles.summary: Georgia is the new No. 1 team in the Associated Press Top 25 poll after Miami's loss to Notre Dame on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Georgia is the new No. 1 team in the Associated Press Top 25 poll after Miami's loss to Notre Dame on Saturday night.

The Bulldogs also bolstered their resume with a 42-7 blowout of Ole Miss. Miami didn't drop too far, moving into No. 5.

Kentucky wasn't so fortunate, going from sixth to 13th following a 34-6 defeat to Tennessee.

Oregon's 41-28 victory over Ohio State was another consequential result, with the team heading in opposite directions. The Ducks are three spots ahead of the Buckeyes.

Saturday's games likely served as a College Football Playoff eliminator for some big teams. Ohio State, LSU, Ole Miss and Missouri all have three defeats now, giving them a narrow and perhaps impossible path to the CFP.

Tigers coach Lane Kiffin isn't on the hot seat already, but the honeymoon period in Baton Rouge is likely over.

If you enter the stadium with an entourage like this, you better win. You certainly can't lose to a rival by 18 points at home.

Thanks to the transfer portal, coaches don't have the grace period they once did. LSU's roster has a reported price tag of $40 million or more. When that's the case, a three-loss season isn't going to cut it.

Things can still get worse for the Tigers, too. They still have to play Texas and Tennessee before wrapping up the regular season against Arkansas.

Even if LSU goes on to post a 9-3 record, Year 1 of the Kiffin era is likely to be deemed a disappointment.

Up north in Columbus, Ohio State coach Ryan Day might finally be running out of time.

Coming up short against USC was bad, but Luke Fahey was making his first career start for an injured Julian Sayin. The Buckeyes still had a lot to play for as well. They almost certainly would've earned a CFP berth as a two-loss team.

Now, that's also off the table, and it will heap even more pressure on Day.

Ohio State has one of the most spoiled fanbases in sports. Going back generations, the Bucks were rarely terrible, and they've been a Top-10 team almost annually since Jim Tressel came aboard in 2001. The 2011 season is the last time they failed to hit 10-plus wins with a full schedule.

Even taking all of that into account, we've reached a point where even Day's most vocal supporters might struggle to make an affirmative argument for him.

The last time Day appeared to be in serious jeopardy, a national title run took a coaching change off the table. That lifeline is in all likelihood off the table given what happened this weekend.

articles.title: Jayden Bogle: Leeds United condemn online racist abuse towards defender after Tottenham game
articles.summary: Leeds United condemn the "disgusting" online racist abuse directed towards defender Jayden Bogle following Saturday's 1-0 win against Tottenham.
articles.body:
Leeds United have condemned the "disgusting" online racist abuse directed towards defender Jayden Bogle following Saturday's 1-0 win against Tottenham .

The 26-year-old Leeds defender was targeted after he escaped punishment for a first-half tackle on Mathys Tel that led to the Spurs forward hobbling off.

The full-back caught the back of Tel's ankle with his studs but referee John Brooks decided not to punish him following a lengthy video assistant referee review.

Tottenham are set to submit a formal complaint about the decision to not send Bogle off and will write to refereeing body Pro Ref to seek an explanation.

Leeds said they had been "appalled" by the racist abuse posted on social media about Bogle, adding it condemned the behaviour "in the strongest possible terms".

"There is no place for racism in football or society," a club statement read.

"The club will work with the Premier League and relevant authorities to identify the individuals and push for the strongest possible action to be taken against them."

Tottenham set to complain to Pro Ref after Bogle escapes red card

Okafor downs Tottenham to earn Leeds first win since September

Bogle reportedly disabled comments on his Instagram account on Saturday after Leeds ' win at Elland Road.

On Sunday, Leeds published a selection of messages Bogle had received - with his permission - to highlight their severity.

"Jayden has the full and unconditional support of the club and his team-mates, and we all stand with him at this time," Leeds added.

"Nobody should ever be subjected to racist abuse."

Tottenham also released a statement , external on Sunday saying the club had been "disgusted" by the abuse suffered by Bogle and have offered their support in identifying those responsible.

"We will pursue every available avenue to ensure they are identified and face the full consequences of their actions," read the statement.

"Regardless of club allegiances and on-pitch results, no-one should ever stand alone in the face of this."

Bogle latest Premier League player to be targeted

It is not the first time this year that Tottenham have had a player, or an opposition player, suffer online racist abuse after a Premier League game.

Tottenham defender Kevin Danso was targeted by "vile" abuse in April, the weekend after Sunderland 's Brian Brobbey had been the subject of racist abuse following an incident in a match against Spurs .

That followed four incidents in February over the same weekend, when Burnley midfielder Hannibal Mejbri, Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana, Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare and Sunderland winger Romaine Mundle were all targeted, which led to a police investigation.

Anti-discrimination group Kick It Out said in April that reports of online abuse were at record levels, increasing by a third compared to the previous season.

At that time, UK Football Policing Unit deputy director Mike Ankers told BBC Radio 5 Live that it had seen an increase of about 115% in the number of reports of online abuse.
